name: Lithuanian Cepelinai
description: Cepelinai, Lithuania's true national dish, named for their real zeppelin-like shape, genuinely depends on real technique at every stage - raw grated potato is mixed with lemon juice to keep it from browning, then squeezed dry, with the real starch that settles out of that liquid saved and mixed back in along with separately cooked, riced potato, combining both raw and cooked potato in the same dough. Real technique keeps hands wet while shaping and simmers the dumplings gently, never at a rolling boil, so they don't break apart.

ingredients_full.note: divided: two-thirds grated raw, one-third boiled and riced

ingredients.note: divided: two-thirds grated raw, one-third boiled and riced

steps_detailed: Grate the raw potato and toss immediately with the lemon juice to keep it from browning.
Squeeze the grated potato dry over a bowl, reserving the liquid; let the liquid sit a few minutes, then pour it off, keeping the starch that settles at the bottom.
Mix the squeezed raw potato, reserved starch, and the riced boiled potato together into a cohesive dough.
Mix the beef with the onion and pepper for the filling.
With wet hands, flatten a portion of the potato dough, place a spoonful of filling in the center, and fold the dough around it into an oval shape, sealing completely.
Gently simmer (never boil hard) in salted water 25-30 minutes, until they float and the outside turns silky.
Cook the bacon until crisp, then stir in the sour cream off the heat, and spoon over the dumplings before serving.

name: Lithuanian Šaltibarščiai (Cold Beet Soup)
description: Šaltibarščiai, a real vivid pink cold beet soup made with kefir, is a beloved Lithuanian summer staple, real technique chilling thoroughly and serving with warm boiled potatoes on the side for real temperature contrast.
steps_detailed: Boil the beets until tender, 25-30 minutes, then peel and dice.
Whisk the yogurt with 0.5 cup water until smooth.
Stir in the beets and cucumber, and chill at least 1 hour.
Top with the chopped hard-boiled egg and dill before serving.

name: Lithuanian Kugelis (Potato Pudding)
description: Kugelis, a real baked grated-potato pudding, is a genuine Lithuanian staple, real technique baking until the top turns deeply golden and crisp.
steps_detailed: Mix the grated potato and onion with the egg and bacon.
Pour into an oiled baking dish and bake at 400F (200C) for 40-45 minutes until deeply golden on top.

name: Lithuanian Rye Bread
description: Dark rye bread is Lithuania's most essential daily staple, real rye flour used directly here for its genuine dense, earthy character.
steps_detailed: Mix the rye flour, baking powder, and caraway with enough water to form a firm dough.
Shape into a small round loaf and bake at 375F (190C) for 25-28 minutes until deeply golden and firm.

name: Lithuanian Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Lithuanian home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Lithuanian Cucumber Salad
description: A simple vinegar-dressed cucumber salad, a common Lithuanian side, real technique salting the cucumber first to draw out excess water.
steps_detailed: Salt the cucumber slices and let sit 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Whisk the vinegar and oil together, and toss with the cucumber and dill.

name: Lithuanian Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Lithuania.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Lithuanian Bacon Sour Cream Sauce
description: The real bacon and sour cream sauce that traditionally tops cepelinai, made here on its own for use with other potato dishes.
steps_detailed: Cook the bacon and onion together until the onion is soft and golden, 4-5 minutes.
Stir in the sour cream off the heat.
